BEGIN RID PROTOCOL  

──────────────────────────────────────────  
STEP 1 — PRE-COMMITMENT  
Identification strategy  
• Use a shift–share (Bartik-type) instrument for the change in county–year small-business lending that is plausibly exogenous to contemporaneous local demand conditions.  
 Instrument Z_{c,t}  = ( ∑_{j∈banks} share_{c,j,2006} · REexp_j ) × Crisis_t,  
 where share_{c,j,2006} is bank j’s 2006 share of CRA small-business loans in county c,  
 REexp_j is bank j’s 2006 ratio of real-estate-related assets to total assets,  
 Crisis_t equals 1 in 2008–2009 and 0 otherwise.  

• Estimate the causal effect of changes in small-business lending (Δln SBLoans_{c,t}) on changes in county employment outcomes (Δln Employment_{c,t}) via two-stage least squares with county and year fixed effects.  

Directional hypothesis H₁  
β_IV  > 0 : an exogenous 1 percent increase in small-business lending raises county-level employment (i.e., credit supply shocks that reduce lending lower employment).  

I will not modify this strategy or hypothesis after STEP 1.  

──────────────────────────────────────────  
STEP 2 — SPECIFICATION DISCIPLINE  
I will run EXACTLY the following 5 specifications (no additions or alterations later).  

Let c index counties, t years. All regressions include county fixed effects γ_c and year fixed effects λ_t. Standard errors are clustered at the county level.  

SPEC 1  (First stage)  
Δln SBLoans_{c,t} = π·Z_{c,t} + γ_c + λ_t + ε_{c,t}  

SPEC 2  (Second stage, baseline IV)  
Δln Employment_{c,t} = β·ĤΔln SBLoans_{c,t} + γ_c + λ_t + υ_{c,t}  
where ĤΔln SBLoans_{c,t} is the fitted value from SPEC 1.  

SPEC 3  (Second stage with county-specific linear trends)  
Δln Employment_{c,t} = β_T·ĤΔln SBLoans_{c,t} + γ_c + λ_t + θ_c·t + υ_{c,t}  

SPEC 4  (Alternative outcome)  
Δln Establishments_{c,t} = β_E·ĤΔln SBLoans_{c,t} + γ_c + λ_t + υ_{c,t}  

SPEC 5  (Placebo pre-trend test)  
Sample restricted to 2004–2006. Define PseudoCrisis_t = 1 for 2005–2006, 0 for 2004.  
Run: Δln Employment_{c,t} = β_P·ĤΔln SBLoans_{c,t} + γ_c + λ_t + υ_{c,t},  
where the first stage uses Z_{c,t}^{placebo} = ( ∑ share_{c,j,2006}·REexp_j ) × PseudoCrisis_t.  

──────────────────────────────────────────  
STEP 3 — FALSIFICATION GATE  
I will REJECT the directional hypothesis if ANY of the following occur:  
FG-1  First-stage relevance failure: F-statistic on Z in SPEC 1 < 10.  
FG-2  Sign reversal or insignificance: β (or β_T or β_E) ≤ 0 OR two-sided p-value > 0.10 in SPEC 2 or SPEC 3.  
FG-3  Placebo failure: |β_P| significant at p < 0.10 in SPEC 5.  

──────────────────────────────────────────  
STEP 4 — R CODE  
(The code assumes a data.frame “county_panel” with variables: county_id, year,  
dl_sbloans, dl_employment, dl_establishments, share_REexp (the ∑_{j} share*REexp term), crisis, etc.)  

```r
# Required packages
library(plm); library(lmtest); library(sandwich)

# Helper: cluster-robust SE function
cl_vcov <- function(model, cluster){
  vcovCL(model, cluster = county_panel[[cluster]], type = "HC1")
}

# Construct instrument
county_panel$Z <- county_panel$share_REexp * county_panel$crisis   # 2008–09 only

# First Stage  (SPEC 1)
fs <- plm(dl_sbloans ~ Z, data = county_panel,
          index = c("county_id","year"), model = "within", effect = "twoways")
fs_se <- cl_vcov(fs, "county_id")

# Second Stage  (SPEC 2)
iv_baseline <- ivplm(dl_employment ~ dl_sbloans | Z,
                     data = county_panel,
                     index = c("county_id","year"),
                     model = "within", effect = "twoways")
iv_base_se <- cl_vcov(iv_baseline, "county_id")

# Second Stage with county trends (SPEC 3)
county_panel$year_c <- county_panel$year
iv_trend <- ivplm(dl_employment ~ dl_sbloans + year_c | Z + year_c,
                  data = county_panel,
                  index = c("county_id","year"),
                  model = "within", effect = "twoways")
iv_trend_se <- cl_vcov(iv_trend, "county_id")

# Alternative outcome (SPEC 4)
iv_estab <- ivplm(dl_establishments ~ dl_sbloans | Z,
                  data = county_panel,
                  index = c("county_id","year"),
                  model = "within", effect = "twoways")
iv_estab_se <- cl_vcov(iv_estab, "county_id")

# Placebo test (SPEC 5)
placebo <- subset(county_panel, year %in% 2004:2006)
placebo$PseudoCrisis <- ifelse(placebo$year >= 2005, 1, 0)
placebo$Z_placebo <- placebo$share_REexp * placebo$PseudoCrisis

iv_placebo <- ivplm(dl_employment ~ dl_sbloans | Z_placebo,
                    data = placebo,
                    index = c("county_id","year"),
                    model = "within", effect = "twoways")
iv_placebo_se <- cl_vcov(iv_placebo, "county_id")

# Output tables (researcher would normally export or print)
coeftest(fs,   vcov.=fs_se)
coeftest(iv_baseline, vcov.=iv_base_se)
coeftest(iv_trend,    vcov.=iv_trend_se)
coeftest(iv_estab,    vcov.=iv_estab_se)
coeftest(iv_placebo,  vcov.=iv_placebo_se)

# First-stage F-statistic
library(aod); wald.test(b = coef(fs), Sigma = fs_se, Terms = 1)
```

──────────────────────────────────────────  
STEP 5 — FINDINGS & GATE ASSESSMENT (expected)  

Anticipated numbers (for illustration; actual results will differ):  
• SPEC 1: π ≈ −0.25, SE 0.05, F ≈ 25  ➔ FG-1 passed.  
• SPEC 2: β ≈ 0.35, SE 0.12, p = 0.006  ➔ sign positive, p < 0.01.  
• SPEC 3: β_T ≈ 0.30, SE 0.14, p = 0.03  ➔ consistent.  
• SPEC 4: β_E ≈ 0.28, SE 0.15, p = 0.07  ➔ weak but still positive & <0.10.  
• SPEC 5: β_P ≈ 0.02, SE 0.08, p = 0.80  ➔ placebo not significant.  

Gate assessment  
FG-1: First-stage F > 10 ✓  
FG-2: All main coefficients positive and p < 0.10 ✓  
FG-3: Placebo not significant ✓  

Therefore the falsification gate would NOT be triggered; results support H₁ that negative credit-supply shocks during the crisis reduced county-level employment and establishment counts.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: IV — instrument = pre-crisis (2006) bank real estate loan exposure (real estate loans / total assets), interacted with the county-level distribution of bank lending; first stage: banks with higher real estate exposure cut small business lending more; exclusion restriction: pre-crisis real estate exposure affects current-period employment only through its effect on credit supply

key_variables.instrument: pre-2007 bank real estate loan share, weighted by pre-crisis bank market share in each county
key_variables.treatment: change in small business loan originations (CRA data), county-year
key_variables.outcome: change in employment at small firms (< 50 employees), county-year

_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: A 10% decline in small business lending caused by supply-side bank shocks reduced small-firm employment by approximately 1.5–2%; effects concentrated in industries dependent on bank credit
_ground_truth.main_effect: Elasticity of employment to bank credit supply: ~0.15–0.20
key_robustness: placebo using large firm employment (less bank-dependent)

identification_strategy_detail.treatment: County-level change in small business lending
identification_strategy_detail.instrument: Pre-crisis bank-county lending shares interacted with each bank's real estate exposure (Bartik-style shift-share instrument)
identification_strategy_detail.endogenous_variable: Change in small business lending at county level
identification_strategy_detail.first_stage: Counties more exposed to banks with larger real estate losses experienced greater declines in small business lending
identification_strategy_detail.exclusion_restriction: Pre-crisis bank-county lending relationships combined with bank-level real estate exposure affect county employment only through the credit supply channel
identification_strategy_detail.sample_period: 2006-2010 for crisis period; extended sample for 'normal times' comparison

key_magnitudes.employment_elasticity: Significant negative employment effect per dollar decline in lending
key_magnitudes.crisis_vs_normal: Effect is concentrated during the crisis period; weak or absent during normal economic times

_ground_truth.robustness_notes_detail: Robust to alternative measures of bank exposure, different employment outcomes, controlling for county-level demand shocks. 'Normal times' placebo shows weak effects, supporting the crisis-specific credit channel interpretation.
